question: Which of the following electrolytes is used in electrolytic refining of copper?
solution:
The correct answer is __**CuSO4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **CuSO4 (Copper(II) sulfate)** is commonly used as the electrolyte in the electrolytic refining of copper.
 
• In the electrolytic refining process, impure copper is used as the anode and pure copper is used as the cathode.
 
• The electrolyte solution is typically an aqueous solution of copper(II) sulfate and sulfuric acid.
 
• During the process, copper ions from the anode dissolve into the solution and are deposited onto the cathode, resulting in pure copper.
 
• This method efficiently removes impurities such as iron, lead, and other metals from the copper.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electrolytic Refining:**

 
 
• A process used to purify metals by electrolysis.
 
• It involves dissolving the impure metal into an electrolyte and depositing the pure metal onto a cathode.
 
 
 
• **Copper(II) Sulfate (CuSO4):**
 
 
• A blue crystalline solid commonly used in electroplating and as a fungicide.
 
• It is soluble in water and forms a blue solution of Cu²⁺ and SO₄²⁻ ions.
 
 
 
• **Anode and Cathode:**
 
 
• **Anode:** The electrode where oxidation occurs (impure copper in refining).
 
• **Cathode:** The electrode where reduction occurs (pure copper in refining).
 
 
 
• **Impurities in Copper:**
 
 
• During electrolytic refining, impurities such as iron, lead, and other metals are removed from copper.
 
• These impurities either remain in the solution or settle as anode sludge.
